# KI-102 — Amend spec §3.1, §14, §15 for local channels

**Lane:** platform · **Complexity:** 1 · **Model:** codex · **Depends on:** KI-101 · **Serializes with:** none
**Plan context (pinned):** [plan](../../../plans/2026-10-02-001-feat-internal-mode-plan.md) · [contracts](../contracts.md) · [roster and graph](../roster.md) · researched at `5ad41c8b`
**Exclusive write surfaces:** `docs/product/khala-spec.md`

## Outcome

`docs/product/khala-spec.md` describes internal mode (product name: **local channel**) as the operator decided it on 2026-10-02 instead of as an open question:

- §3.1 states the scope (D1), the on-demand loopback helper (D2), the exact no-egress wording (D3), the full web app served locally (D4), joining (D5), persistence (D6) and identity (D8), and that agent-created channels are human-directed (the owner asks the agent in that turn).
- §4.4 no longer says the human interface is undecided.
- §14 "Internal operation" names the narrowed, testable no-egress outcome.
- §15 marks "Local no-egress guarantee" and "Internal agent-created channels" as decided, pointing at §3.1.

Docs-only. No code, test or other document changes.

## Context and evidence

- Plan Goal Capsule: "Product Contract preservation: spec §3.1 changes per D2/D3 (KI-102 edits the spec). §14 'Internal operation' gains the narrowed no-egress wording and its automated check." Plan U2: "Rewrite §3.1 (lines 42-54) and the §14 'Internal operation' row (line ~377) and the §15 'Local no-egress guarantee' row to D2/D3; record D1–D8." (The §14 row is at line 380 at `5ad41c8b`.)
- Operator decisions, verbatim from the plan (Key Decisions):
  - **D1 Scope:** same machine first — one human, Claude + Codex on one machine. Cross-machine/tailnet is a later phase (out of this plan except a short follow-on note).
  - **D2 Transport:** on-demand loopback helper `khala local serve` on 127.0.0.1 only, started automatically by the khala CLI/agent when a local channel is created/used, never installed as a service, exits when idle; single writer of an append-only per-channel log in the khala state dir; amend spec §3.1 wording accordingly.
  - **D3 No-egress wording:** "No Khala servers, no sign-in; messages are stored only on this machine. Each agent's model provider sees what that agent reads." + an automated test that Khala opens zero non-loopback connections in local mode; fix landing card copy accordingly.
  - **D4 Human UI:** the FULL web app — the same exact UI and functionality as khala.aiur.team, served locally by the helper. … Local "owner" mode skips Google sign-in and uses a local profile (username, initials, colour, agent names, listener modes all work locally).
  - **D5 Join:** single-use 10-minute link, auto-join on loopback (no confirm click); join announced in channel; removable.
  - **D6 Persistence:** channels persist on disk until deleted; no auto-prune in MVP.
  - **D8 Identity:** local owner name from cached hosted username if present, else $USER; agents `<name>-Claude`/`<name>-Codex` with -2 on collision using the shared name validator; never fetched from or written to the hosted profile.
- Why the old text must change:
  - `docs/product/khala-spec.md:48` forbids "a mandatory local web server … by default". D2 resolves it: the helper is on demand, loopback only, never a service, and exits when idle, so nothing is mandatory or running by default.
  - `docs/product/khala-spec.md:52` asks the design to "show how participating agents satisfy the stated no-egress requirement, or explicitly surface the conflict for a scope decision". D3 is that scope decision: Khala's own traffic stays on loopback (tested, KI-151) and the copy discloses that each agent's model provider sees what that agent reads.
  - `docs/product/khala-spec.md:54` and `:100` leave the local human interface open and say a full duplicate of the website is "not required". D4 chose the full web app, served locally, through a port seam rather than a copy.
  - `docs/product/khala-spec.md:50` and `:397` keep agent-created internal channels as an open candidate. Plan flow F1 (Claude runs `khala local create` when the owner asks) settles it as human-directed creation.
- D7 (delete `apps/internal`) is a repository decision, not product behaviour, and is not written into the spec.

## Contract and invariants

This ticket consumes no wire shape. It states product facts that later tickets implement; the numbers it quotes must equal contracts.md L3 and L11, verbatim:

```ts
export const LOCAL_DEFAULT_PORT = 47830;
export const LOCAL_LINK_TTL_MS = 600_000;                                // single-use share link and open link lifetime (D5)
export const LOCAL_IDLE_EXIT_MS = 600_000;                               // helper exits after 10 min with no request and no open long-poll (D2)
```

> - Binds `127.0.0.1` only, port `KHALA_LOCAL_PORT` or `LOCAL_DEFAULT_PORT` (47830). …
> - **Idle exit (D2):** the helper exits 0 after `KHALA_LOCAL_IDLE_MS` (default `LOCAL_IDLE_EXIT_MS`) with no request and no open long-poll. It is never installed as a service.

Invariants:
- The D3 sentence appears in §3.1 **verbatim**, character for character: `No Khala servers, no sign-in; messages are stored only on this machine. Each agent's model provider sees what that agent reads.` (straight apostrophes, semicolon after "sign-in").
- The spec must not claim "no chat leaves the computer" or anything stronger than D3.
- The spec states no product behaviour beyond D1–D8 and the plan's F1 creation flow (no new limits, no new settings).
- Section numbers, headings and table column structure are unchanged, so existing links into the spec keep working.

**2. §3.1** — keep line 42 `### 3.1 Internal mode — confirmed scope`, replace lines 44-54 with:

```markdown
Internal mode is a minimal, local protocol for **one human and their multiple local agents on one computer** to communicate. Product copy calls it a **local channel**. The first release covers one human with Claude Code and Codex sessions on the same computer; cross-machine local channels are a later phase.

It must not require third-party hosting, external services, Khala servers, sign-in, a database or additional runtime dependencies. It must not depend on the Khala website, Gmail sign-in, or external channel infrastructure to operate.

**Transport.** One on-demand helper, `khala local serve`, listens on 127.0.0.1 only. The `khala` CLI or agent starts it automatically when a local channel is created or used; it is never installed as a service, and it exits when idle. It is the single writer of an append-only log per channel in the Khala state directory. This satisfies "no mandatory server by default": nothing runs until a local channel is used, and nothing listens beyond loopback.

**Human interface.** The human uses the full Khala web app, with the same screens and functions as khala.aiur.team, served locally by the helper. It is the existing app running against a local adapter, not a copy. Local owner mode skips Google sign-in and keeps a local profile: username, initials, colour, agent names and listener modes all work locally.

**Joining.** An agent joins with a single-use link that expires after 10 minutes. On this computer the join completes without a confirmation click, the join is announced in the channel, and the human can remove the agent.

**Persistence.** Local channels stay on disk until the human deletes them. Nothing is pruned automatically.

**Identity.** The local owner name is the cached hosted username when one exists, else the operating-system user name (`$USER`). Agents are named `<name>-Claude` and `<name>-Codex`, with `-2` on collision, using the shared name validator. Local identity is never fetched from or written to the hosted profile.

**Channel creation.** Human-directed channel creation is in scope. The human creates a local channel in the web app, or asks one of their agents in their own turn to create it; the agent then returns the links. Agents do not create local channels on their own initiative, and there is no setting that lets them.

**No-egress promise.** User-facing copy states exactly: "No Khala servers, no sign-in; messages are stored only on this machine. Each agent's model provider sees what that agent reads." Khala's own processes (the helper, each agent's Khala integration and the local web app) open no non-loopback connection in local mode, and an automated test proves it. Content an agent reads goes to that agent's model provider; the copy discloses this instead of promising that no content leaves the computer.

Encryption of local files beyond owner-only file permissions is not part of this scope. None of these decisions authorizes adding cloud dependencies.
```

The local interface is the full web app served by an on-demand loopback helper. Running agents only on local models is a possible later option, not a requirement. |

## Test scenarios

No test file exists for the spec (`git grep -n "khala-spec" -- '*.ts' '*.mjs'` is empty at `5ad41c8b`). The checks are textual; run them from the repo root:

1. `grep -cF "No Khala servers, no sign-in; messages are stored only on this machine. Each agent's model provider sees what that agent reads." docs/product/khala-spec.md` → `1`.
2. `grep -n "mandatory local web server" docs/product/khala-spec.md` → no output.
3. `grep -n "open candidate feature\|Important unresolved boundary\|still a design decision" docs/product/khala-spec.md` → no output.
4. `grep -n "^| Internal operation |" docs/product/khala-spec.md` → exactly one line, containing `zero non-loopback connections`.
